memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I give to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as their inheritance in return for the work they do while serving at the tent of meeting. From now on the Israelites must not go near the tent of meeting, or they will bear the consequences of their sin and will die. It is the Levites who are to do the work at the tent of meeting and bear the responsibility for any offenses they commit against it. This is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come. They will receive no inheritance among the Israelites." — Num 18:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God arranged that the Levites, who had no farmland of their own, would be supported by the tithes of the people. Because they gave their lives to serving God on behalf of everyone, the community provided for their needs. It was a picture of God's people caring for those who minister among them.

There is a healthy interdependence built into God's design. The Levites served the whole nation spiritually; the nation supported them materially. Neither could function without the other. God did not intend His servants to be neglected, nor His people to receive spiritual care without also giving in return. Everyone had a part to play.

This principle carries forward into the New Testament. Paul teaches that those who preach the gospel should be supported by those they serve, "just as the Levites of old were provided for." Caring for those who give themselves to God's work is not optional generosity but part of God's good order for His people. When we support those who minister, we share in their work.

Yet even here we are pointed higher. The Levites served, but imperfectly, needing to bear responsibility for their own offenses. Christ, our great High Priest, served perfectly and needed no one to atone for Him. He gave Himself entirely to the work of our salvation, receiving nothing but a cross in return. In gratitude, we gladly support His work and His servants today, remembering the One who gave everything for us and asked nothing back but our hearts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you support those who give themselves to God's work?
2. How does God's design of interdependence shape the way you view His people?
3. How does Christ's selfless service move you to generosity?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for those who give their lives to serving You and Your people. Help me to support and honour them as part of Your good design. Thank You for Christ, who gave everything for me and asked only for my heart. Amen.
